question: Does one constant hidden direction survive the native QuickGELU-to-c_proj derivative across fixed actual MNIST inputs?
scope: Necessary local operator diagnostic, not a protection, classification experiment, or repetition of paired nonlinear shear
site: block0 MLP c_fc output and unchanged c_proj
family: E1=v a^T with a=normalized mean native LN2 input; b1 and W2 unchanged. A valid output-complement candidate would additionally require P_z v=0 and bounded finite native error. Neither is assumed.
condition: For exact local-output preservation along every sufficiently small alpha, t_s W2 diag(QuickGELUprime(z_s)) v=0 for every native context, t_s=a^T x_s. Inspect a permissive unconstrained v first, before any task-complement restriction.
context_selection: First three images in each declared training split; CLS and patch token24, six fit and six untouched confirmation contexts; no partner or test access.
device: Existing RTX3090 only; FP32 model forwards, FP64 operator algebra, TF32 disabled
rank_reporting: Report full singular spectrum extrema and fixed eps*max(shape)*smax tolerance; also report relative1e-8 numerical rank. Neither cutoff chooses a protection rank.
stable_regime: Fixed-sign ReLU approximation requires W2 D v=0; report rank of columns for neurons positive on all fit and confirmation tokens. No margin fitting.
stop: No weights regardless of rank. Full numerical rank only rules out an exact local infinitesimal null direction for this fixed input scalar/site, not approximate accuracy preservation, finite discrete equivalences, paired edits, or all complement methods. If weak directions are low-activity or confirmation responses grow, do not call them a new candidate. Public cleanup utility has not been established.
classification_metrics: Not measured: target/partner native and fusion accuracies, AGA and cleanup. No defense efficacy claim permitted.
